issues: Source 1 cited Wikipedia ('Semayne's case') for the standard-report wording 'as well for his defence'. It is replaced with the U.S. Supreme Court's opinion in Wilson v. Layne (1999), which quotes that wording from 77 Eng. Rep. 194, 5 Co. Rep. 91a, 91b and dates the case to 1604 (--check FOUND).

sourceFixes.institution: Supreme Court of the United States (via Cornell LII)
sourceFixes.title: Wilson v. Layne, 526 U.S. 603 (1999), opinion of the Court (Rehnquist C.J.)
sourceFixes.quote: In 1604, an English court made the now-famous observation that "the house of every one is to him as his castle and fortress, as well for his defence against injury and violence, as for his repose."
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation (Semayne's case). --check FOUND on 2026-09-23. The opinion cites 'Semayne's Case, 77 Eng. Rep. 194, 5 Co. Rep. 91a, 91b, 195 (K. B.)'. It confirms the standard report's 'for his defence' reading mentioned in the record's note; the Liberty Fund text (source 0) reads 'for defence'. The Court calls it the observation of 'an English court', which fits the speaker field: Coke reported the King's Bench resolution but did not decide it.
